title: Peak: How Great Companies Get Their Mojo From Maslow

questions.q: What perk does Chip Conley give his hotel employees?
a: Free stays at the company's hotels, up to four times a year
Cash bonuses tied to each quarter's profits
Extra paid vacation days every few months
Free meals in the hotel restaurants each day
questions.why: Lesson 1 describes free stays as a way for employees to experience the value they create firsthand.

questions.q: How does Café Gratitude try to offer more than a good meal?
a: Servers ask guests thoughtful, personal questions
Servers memorize each guest's usual order
Guests receive discounts for returning soon
Guests fill out a survey before they leave
questions.why: Lesson 2 describes waiters asking questions about gratitude and important people in guests' lives.

questions.q: What does Conley compare the process of getting investors to?
a: Dating, from casual encounters to marriage
Hiring, from first interviews to long careers
Coaching, from basic drills to real games
Farming, from planting season to harvest
questions.why: Lesson 3 opens with the comparison that raising money is like dating and choosing whom to marry.

questions.q: Why does Conley send his investors an annual survey?
a: To learn their priorities and what they want
To announce the next year's room rates
To gather feedback on hotel service
To confirm the size of their ownership stakes
questions.why: Lesson 3 says the only way to know what investors want is to ask them, so he surveys them each year.

questions.q: What did Conley send investors along with the bleak 2001 financial report?
a: A joke t-shirt about buying a San Francisco hotel
A personal letter offering his resignation
A free weekend stay at one of the hotels
A detailed recovery plan with strict deadlines
questions.why: Lesson 3 describes the t-shirt saying that all he got was a lousy T-shirt, sent to show his humor.
